title: Tree to fan-in-two circuit size bound
statement: Let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and let $L$ be a language of Boolean words. If for every input length $n$ there is a Boolean circuit tree of size at most $T(n)$ that accepts exactly the words of length $n$ in $L$, then there is a family of well-formed acyclic Boolean circuits with fan-in at most two that recognizes $L$ and has size at most $n+3T(n)$ on inputs of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
$L$ is a language of Boolean words
$L$ has Boolean circuit trees of size at most $T(n)$ recognizing it at each length
